edition.text: Later collected text, as in the 1955 Hawthorn edition
edition.note: The Lessons follow the standard collected text. Its tale "The Clay Tablets From Babylon" carries letters dated October 21, 1934 and November 7th, 1936, so that tale cannot come from a 1926 printing. Open Library (https://openlibrary.org/books/OL6175371M) lists a 1955 Hawthorn edition under this title; a Wikipedia talk-page note says the pamphlets began in 1926 and the book under this title appeared in 1955. Which printing first held all the tales was not established from a primary source.

rows.claim: This Lesson distils the Five Laws of Gold and the later tales: the gold lender, the camel trader and the clay tablets. For an index investor they are rules on where €40k may safely go, and where it may not.
rows.note: The table of contents shows "The Five Laws of Gold", "The Gold Lender of Babylon", "The Camel Trader of Babylon" and "The Clay Tablets From Babylon". The €40k is the reader's own roadmap sum, not a figure from the book. Card unchanged.
